_note.name: Why this case has no unit-level proxy
_note.note: The Parks Inspection Program rates DPR property only, and it never rates a plaza. Entries 0 and 1 are the 2 city sources that define the plaza set, and neither one rates condition. Thus the plazas case can compare the model against the AREA only. It cannot test the model against an inspector, the way the parks, schools, and restaurants cases can. Search for a plaza condition source before you read a weak correlation here as a finding about the model.

4.name: Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS) — year completed
4.note: The vintage of a plaza. This is the year of the SPACE, not of the tower beside it, thus it describes the plaza directly. It reaches 347 of the 392 POPS units (88.5%); the other 45 carry a BBL that the POPS table does not hold. WARNING: 1 plaza source of 3 has a year. The 92 DOT pedestrian plazas and the 20 city-state parks carry no vintage in any NYC source, thus this proxy covers 68.8% of the case. WARNING: a year is not oriented.
